meta.route: New York → Beijing → Xi'an → Beijing → New York
meta.budget_total: ≈ US$2,340 (mid, 1 traveller, excl. visa fee — see budget)
meta.self_check: self-checked: 11 issues found and fixed — Monday closure of the Palace Museum (route reversed so Beijing lands on Tue), the 15/16 Nov winter-hours switch (per-day hours re-checked on both sides), Terracotta last ticket vs arrival, Temple of Heaven 16:30 last admission vs a 15:35 arrival, Shaanxi History Museum Monday closure, day-7 walking cut from 9.2 to 7.6 km, 6 hop rows added so every stop-to-stop transition carries its own map link, two lodging stops renamed to clear a name-collision warning, sunset prose aligned to the sun tool, the return-day clock rewritten as a formula instead of a guessed departure time, and the 240-hour transit waiver ruled out before the visa line was written.
meta.assumption: HEADLESS RUN — no checkpoint was possible, so the route skeleton was chosen for you: Xi'an first, Beijing second. See decisions.

decisions: Tourist (L) visa, not visa-free transit. China's 240-hour transit waiver needs a third country (A → China → B). A JFK → China → JFK round trip is A → China → A, so it does NOT qualify — you must hold an L visa before you fly.

Xi'an first, Beijing second. This puts the Great Wall on a Monday and the Forbidden City on a Tuesday: the Palace Museum is closed Mondays anyway, its 40,000/day tickets are far easier to catch on a weekday, and the trip ends in the city that has your international airport.

High-speed rail both ways instead of flying out of Xi'an. 4 h 10–5 h city-centre to city-centre beats a separate-ticket XIY→PEK connection (which would need a 4 h self-transfer buffer) and keeps one round-trip international ticket.
Only two hotels for six nights — no one-night stays, no repacking mid-trip.
The Great Wall day deliberately carries ONE anchor instead of three. Mutianyu is a 2 h ride each way plus 3–4 h on the wall; anything else on that day is a lie.
Food is written as areas (Muslim Quarter, Gui Jie, Qianmen), never as named restaurants — Chinese street-food stalls churn faster than any plan can track.

checklist.item: Chinese tourist visa (L) — apply at the Chinese Visa Application Service Center via the COVA online form, then submit the passport in person
checklist.deadline: start 8 weeks out (by 2026-09-16); passport is held for the whole processing window
checklist.price: fee reduced through 2026-12-31 — ⚠️ exact amount unverified, read it at the link (express +$25)
checklist.note: Since 2024-01-01 no round-trip ticket, hotel booking, itinerary or invitation letter is required for L visas filed in the US. Most US citizens get a 10-year multiple-entry visa. Passport: 6+ months validity, 2 blank pages.

checklist.item: 12306 account + passport identity verification (China Railway official)
checklist.deadline: do it now — verification can take days; tickets release 15 days ahead at 14:00 Beijing time
checklist.note: Beijing↔Xi'an tickets for 2026-11-12 open ~2026-10-28 14:00 CST (2026-10-28 01:00 EST). Visa/Mastercard accepted. Book with the SAME passport you will travel on.

checklist.item: Forbidden City (Palace Museum) timed ticket for 2026-11-17
checklist.deadline: 2026-11-10, 20:00 Beijing time = 2026-11-10 07:00 EST — 7 days ahead, to the minute
checklist.note: Online only, no walk-up window, 40,000/day cap, real-name against your passport number. Bring the original passport to the Meridian Gate. Sets an alarm-clock task, not a to-do.

checklist.item: Tiananmen Square entry reservation for 2026-11-17 (separate from the Palace Museum)
checklist.deadline: opens ~7 days ahead; book the same morning you book the Palace Museum
checklist.note: ⚠️ Channel unverified (WeChat mini-program 天安门广场预约 is the usual route and has no English UI). Fallback: skip the square, enter the Palace Museum directly from the east side.

checklist.item: Terracotta Army (Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum) ticket for 2026-11-13
checklist.deadline: bookable 30+ days out; buy as soon as the visa is granted
checklist.price: ¥120 (≈$17.80) — includes the three pits + Lishan Garden
checklist.note: Original passport required at the gate — photocopies and phone photos are refused.

checklist.item: Shaanxi History Museum free reservation for 2026-11-14
checklist.note: ⚠️ WeChat official account only, no English version, daily cap. If it fails, the plan swaps in Xi'an Museum / Small Wild Goose Pagoda (free, open Sat) — already written into rain_alt.

checklist.item: Alipay and/or WeChat Pay installed and an international Visa/Mastercard linked
checklist.deadline: before departure — verification needs a working phone number
checklist.note: China is effectively cashless. Alipay is the more foreigner-friendly of the two. Carry ¥500–1000 cash as a hard backup anyway; legally every vendor must accept it.

checklist.item: Roaming travel eSIM (Airalo / Holafly / Saily style) — NOT a local China SIM
checklist.deadline: buy before departure, activate on landing
checklist.note: A roaming eSIM tunnels out of mainland China, so Google Maps / Gmail / WhatsApp keep working. A local SIM sits behind the Great Firewall. See the connectivity note in the country brief — this is the single highest-leverage $20 on the trip.

checklist.item: Travel medical insurance with evacuation cover
checklist.note: Chinese public hospitals expect payment up front from foreigners.

checklist.item: Mutianyu access for 2026-11-16 — confirm the Dongzhimen tourist coach is still running
checklist.note: ⚠️ The seasonal 慕田峪 direct coach from Dongzhimen thins out after mid-November. Backup: DiDi/private car (~1 h 20 each way) — book the return leg too, hailing from the wall car park is unreliable.

checklist.item: Re-confirm every opening hour, last-entry time and fee
checklist.note: These dates are 3 months out: what is verified below is the SEASONAL PATTERN as of 2026-08-15, not that specific day's published hours. Mutianyu and the Terracotta Army both flip to winter hours on 2026-11-16 — mid-trip.

legs.price: $983 round trip incl. the 2026-11-18 return (Google Flights cache, as of 2026-08-15 — comparison grade, confirm at the link)
legs.bags: 1 × 23 kg checked included on Korean Air transpacific economy ⚠️ verify fare-class at booking
legs.backup: Air China nonstop JFK→PEK (~13 h 50) — shorter and no Seoul transfer, price unverified; also compare Beijing Daxing (PKX) arrivals, but PKX adds ~40 min to the city.

legs.price: ¥515.5 second class / ¥824.5 first (≈$76 / $122) — travelchinaguide, as of 2026-08-15
legs.bags: no fee, but you carry it yourself up and down platforms
legs.backup: 23+ G-trains a day, last departure 19:00 — if the flight lands late, rebook onto a later train on the 12306 app rather than eating the fare.
an 08:00 departure buys an extra hour in Beijing; a 10:00 one buys a calmer morning.

legs.dep: ⚠️ time not verified — read it off your ticket, then work backwards
legs.arr: same calendar day in New York (you cross the date line eastbound)
legs.backup: Leave the hotel at departure minus 4 h 15 (3 h international check-in + 75 min city→PEK T3). Day 8's timeline is written against that formula, not against a guessed time.

days.label: Departure
days.ribbon: JFK T1 →Korean Air 00:50→ Seoul ICN →connect→ Beijing PEK (lands 09:25 on the 12th)
days.rain_alt: none needed — the whole day is indoors
days.late_cut: missed the 00:50 departure → Korean Air rebooks onto the next ICN service; the Xi'an train on day 2 is the piece to move, and 12306 lets you change it in-app.

timeline.what: Leave Manhattan for JFK — AirTrain + LIRR, or a car. A 00:50 departure means you check in on the evening of the 10th.
JFK Terminal 1 — check in, clear security. Last chance to install the eSIM profile, Alipay and a VPN while you are still outside the Great Firewall.
timeline.note: Do NOT plan to download these in China. Half of them are unreachable from a Chinese IP.

timeline.what: Korean Air JFK → Seoul ICN → Beijing PEK · ~19 h 35 total incl. connection
timeline.note: 13 h ahead of New York. Sleep on the transpacific leg, stay awake after the Seoul connection — you land at 09:25 and the day has barely started.

days.label: Landing, and straight onto the rails
days.ribbon: PEK T3 →car 75′→ 北京西 →G-train ~4h30→ 西安北 →metro L2 30′→ 南院门 hotel →walk 13′→ 回民街
days.rain_alt: the whole day is a corridor — rain changes nothing except taking the metro instead of walking the last 600 m
days.late_cut: flight lands late → do NOT sprint. Change the G-ticket in the 12306 app to any later departure (they run to 19:00); worst case sleep in Beijing and take the 06:38 tomorrow, dropping Huaqing Palace from day 3.

timeline.what: Land PEK Terminal 3 · immigration (fingerprints for first-time entrants), bags, customs
timeline.note: Budget the full 80 min. Turn the eSIM on before immigration so you can call a car the moment you clear.

timeline.what: Car PEK T3 → Beijing West Railway Station 北京西 · ~55 km · 65-90 min · ¥130-170
timeline.note: Airport Express + Line 2 + Line 9 is ¥32 and ~95 min with two changes and stairs. With a suitcase and 13 h of jet lag, take the car.

timeline.what: Beijing West — passport gate (orange lane, tap the passport), lunch inside the station, find the waiting hall
timeline.note: Beijing West is enormous and signage assumes you can read Chinese. 90 min is not padding.

timeline.what: G-train 北京西 → 西安北 · ~4 h 30 · ¥515.5 second class
timeline.note: Reserved seat, no standing. Trolley service is thin — buy food at the station.

timeline.what: Metro Line 2 西安北 → 南院门 (Bell Tower stn, 1 block) · ~30 min · ¥5
timeline.note: Line 2 runs from directly under the station concourse to the middle of the walled city.

timeline.what: Hotel check-in, drop the bag, wash your face
Walk 南院门 → 回民街 Muslim Quarter · 0.9 km · 13 min — the first meal: roujiamo, biangbiang noodles, persimmon cakes
Muslim Quarter — eat standing up, then walk back past the lit Drum Tower. Bed early; tomorrow starts at 08:00.

days.label: The Qin emperor's army

walking_km.how: inside the three pits ~3.0 + Lishan Garden 1.0 + Huaqing Palace grounds 1.6 + station walks 0.5 ×1.3

days.ribbon: 南院门 →bus 游5 70′→ 秦始皇帝陵博物院 →walk 8′→ food street →shuttle 20′→ 华清宫 →bus 65′→ 南院门
days.rain_alt: Pit 1 and Pit 3 are fully roofed; the walk between pits is covered. If it turns wet, cut Huaqing Palace (mostly outdoor gardens) and take the Shaanxi History Museum slot from tomorrow instead.
days.late_cut: running >1 h late → drop Huaqing Palace, not the museum. Getting back before dark matters more than the Tang bathing pools.

timeline.what: Hotel breakfast. Pack the passport — it is checked at the museum gate, not just at booking.
Bus 游5 (306) from the station east square → 秦始皇帝陵博物院 · ~70 min · ¥8
timeline.note: The official 游5 has a green-and-white livery and a queue marshal. Ignore the touts working the same forecourt — private minibuses with the same number are a known scam.

timeline.what: Emperor Qinshihuang's Mausoleum Site Museum 秦始皇帝陵博物院 — Pit 1 (the army), Pit 3 (the command post), Pit 2 (the kneeling archer), then the Bronze Chariots hall
timeline.note: 08:30-18:30 to 15 Nov, ticket check closes 17:00 (from 16 Nov: 08:30-18:00, check closes 16:30). Enter Pit 1 from the back-right corner and walk against the crowd. Original passport required.

timeline.what: Walk 秦始皇帝陵博物院 → 兵马俑小吃街 food street · 0.5 km · 8 min
Lunch — the food street outside the museum gate · noodles and roujiamo, tourist-priced but fine

timeline.what: Shuttle bus 兵马俑 → 华清宫 · 6 km · ~20 min · ¥5
Huaqing Palace 华清宫 — the Tang imperial hot springs, the Xi'an Incident rooms on the hillside behind
timeline.note: 07:00-18:00 to 30 Nov, ticket check to 17:10. The Li Mountain cable car is a separate fee and not worth it in November haze.

timeline.what: Bus 游5 (306) 华清宫 → 南院门 (via Xi'an station) · ~65 min · ¥7
timeline.note: Last 游5 back leaves around 18:00-19:00 in winter — do not test it.

timeline.what: Back at the hotel — shower, reset. Sunset is 17:43 and it gets cold fast.
Dinner around the Bell Tower / 东木头市 · dumplings, yangrou paomo · a local street, not the tourist one

days.label: On the wall, under the pagoda

walking_km.how: hotel→South Gate 1.3 + museum→pagoda 1.2 + pagoda→Everbright 0.6 ×1.3 + inside the museum 1.5 + on the wall 0.5 (the 13.7 km loop is ridden, not walked)

days.ribbon: 南院门 →walk 13′→ 永宁门 (ride the 13.7 km loop) →metro→ 回民街 lunch →metro 35′→ 陕西历史博物馆 →walk 18′→ 大雁塔 →walk 9′→ 大唐不夜城 →metro 25′→ 南院门
days.rain_alt: the wall is exposed and the bikes stop in rain — swap it for Xi'an Museum / Small Wild Goose Pagoda 小雁塔 (free, open Sat, closed Tue) and give the pagoda district the whole afternoon.
days.late_cut: running late → ride only the south-to-west quarter of the wall (45 min) instead of the full loop; the museum's last admission is the hard stop.

timeline.what: Walk 南院门 → 永宁门 City Wall South Gate · 0.9 km · 13 min
Xi'an City Wall 西安城墙 — ride the full 13.7 km circuit on a rental bike, anticlockwise from the South Gate
timeline.note: Gates open 08:00 (South Gate to 23:00; other gates 08:00-18:00 Nov-Apr). The full loop is ~2 h at a gentle pace with photo stops. The paving is uneven — brakes, not speed.

timeline.what: Metro Line 2 永宁门 → 回民街 (Bell Tower stn + 600 m walk) · ~25 min · ¥2
Lunch, Muslim Quarter 回民街 + 化觉巷 — the alley behind the Great Mosque is where locals eat
timeline.note: Cash is genuinely useless here; every stall takes Alipay/WeChat QR.

timeline.what: Metro Line 2 回民街 → 陕西历史博物馆 (钟楼→小寨 + walk) · ~35 min · ¥3
Shaanxi History Museum 陕西历史博物馆 — the Zhou/Qin/Han/Tang galleries; the Tang mural hall is a separate paid ticket
timeline.note: ⚠️ Reservation-only via a Chinese-language WeChat account and it sells out in minutes. 09:00-17:30 from 15 Nov, last admission 16:30; today (14 Nov) is the last 08:30-18:00 day. Closed Mondays.
timeline.tag: swap→Xi'an Museum 小雁塔 (free, no booking fight)

timeline.what: Walk 陕西历史博物馆 → 大雁塔 · 1.2 km · 18 min
Big Wild Goose Pagoda 大雁塔 / Da Ci'en Temple — the Tang pagoda Xuanzang built to house the sutras he carried back from India; climb it for the sunset over the Tang city grid
timeline.note: 08:00-17:00 winter, last climb ~16:30. Sunset today 17:42 (route_tools sun).

timeline.what: Walk 大雁塔 → 大唐不夜城 Datang Everbright City · 0.6 km · 9 min
Datang Everbright City 大唐不夜城 at dusk — a free open-air Tang-revival street, lit from ~17:30, with street performers and the food arcades off the main axis
Dinner in the Datang arcades or back at 永兴坊 · Shaanxi small plates
Metro Line 2/3 大唐不夜城 → 南院门 · ~25 min · ¥3

days.label: North again, and a circle of blue tiles

walking_km.how: Temple of Heaven park axis 2.6 + Qianmen / Dashilan 1.2 ×1.3 + station walks 0.3

days.ribbon: 南院门 →metro 35′→ 西安北 →G-train ~4h30→ 北京西 →metro 35′→ 鲜鱼口 hotel →metro 25′→ 天坛东门 →walk/metro 25′→ 前门大街
days.rain_alt: the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests is outdoors — swap the Temple of Heaven for the National Museum of China on Tiananmen Square (free, reservation required, closed Mondays) and keep the Qianmen evening.
days.late_cut: train late → drop the Temple of Heaven entirely (attractions shut at 17:00) and spend the evening on Qianmen and Dashilan instead; the park is a fine morning substitute on day 7 if you skip Jingshan.

timeline.what: Checkout, metro Line 2 南院门 → 西安北 · ~35 min · ¥5
Xi'an North — passport gate, waiting hall, coffee
timeline.note: Chinese stations close boarding 3-5 min before departure. 30 min before is the real deadline, not a suggestion.

timeline.what: G-train 西安北 → 北京西 · ~4 h 30 · ¥515.5 second class
Metro Line 9 → Line 7 北京西 → 鲜鱼口 · ~35 min · ¥5
Hotel check-in, drop the bag
Metro/foot 鲜鱼口 → 天坛东门 Temple of Heaven East Gate · ~25 min · ¥3
Temple of Heaven 天坛 — the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests, the Echo Wall, the Circular Mound Altar, walked north to south down the raised causeway
timeline.note: Park 06:30-22:00; the MONUMENTS are 08:00-17:00 with last admission 16:30 (1 Nov-31 Mar). Arriving 15:35 is enough for the axis, not for lingering. Sunset in Beijing 16:59 — note the day's sun line is computed from the day's FIRST stop, which is still Xi'an (17:41).

timeline.what: Walk out of the park's west gate → 前门大街 Qianmen Street · ~25 min
Qianmen Street 前门大街 and the Dashilan 大栅栏 lanes — the restored Qing shopfront street, the old lanes behind it, and roast duck for dinner
timeline.note: Qianmen itself is a tourist street; the food is one block west in Dashilan and Xianyukou.

days.label: The wall, on a Monday

walking_km.how: wall towers 14→20 and back down to the toboggan 2.6 + base street and stairs 1.5 ×1.3 (the cable car up and the toboggan down are ridden)

days.ribbon: 鲜鱼口 →metro 30′→ 东直门 →coach 100′→ 慕田峪 →shuttle+cable car→ 14号敌楼 →walk 35′→ 正关台 →toboggan→ 慕田峪村 →coach 120′→ 鲜鱼口
days.rain_alt: the cable car and toboggan shut in high wind or ice. Wet-day swap: the Summer Palace 颐和园 (¥30, corridors and halls are covered) plus the 798 art district — both indoor-ish and both open Mondays.
days.late_cut: on the wall past 14:30 → skip Tower 20 and take the cable car back down from Tower 14 rather than the toboggan; the last cable car is 17:00 and the last coach out is earlier than you think.

timeline.what: Early breakfast, metro Line 2 鲜鱼口 → 东直门 Dongzhimen · ~30 min · ¥4
Coach 东直门 → 慕田峪游客中心 Mutianyu · ~90-110 min · ≈¥60 return
timeline.note: ⚠️ The seasonal direct coach thins after mid-November — confirmed on the checklist. Backup: DiDi ~¥350 each way, ~80 min. Monday means no weekend queue at either end.

timeline.what: 慕田峪游客中心 → 14号敌楼 Tower 14 — passport ticket check, shuttle bus, cable car up · ~30 min
timeline.price: ¥45 entry + ¥15 shuttle + ¥140 cable car return / ¥120 up + toboggan down
timeline.note: From today the scenic area runs winter hours 08:00-17:30 and the cable car 08:00-17:00.

timeline.what: Mutianyu Great Wall 慕田峪长城 — Tower 14 and the restored western ramparts, the forested Huairou ridge dropping away on both sides
timeline.note: This is the day's only anchor and that is the point. Mutianyu is forested, less restored-to-death than Badaling, and on a November Monday you will have long stretches of it alone. Steep steps, uneven treads — proper shoes.

timeline.what: Walk the ramparts 14号敌楼 → 正关台 Tower 20 · 0.9 km of steps · 35 min
Zhengguantai 正关台 — the three-tower crown at the top of the restored section, then back down the wall westward
timeline.note: This and the block above are one anchor split by the ridge walk. On a November Monday you will have long stretches of it alone. Steep steps, uneven treads — proper shoes.

timeline.what: Toboggan 滑道 正关台 → 慕田峪村 base village (or the cable car if it is icy) · ~20 min
Late lunch at the Mutianyu base village — trout, farm greens, hand-pulled noodles
Coach 慕田峪村 → 鲜鱼口 (via Dongzhimen) · ~2 h
timeline.note: Leaving by 15:00 keeps you out of the Beijing evening jam.

timeline.what: Back at the hotel — feet up. The wall is a 20,000-step day even when the map says 5 km.
Dinner on Gui Jie 簋街 (Dongzhimennei Dajie) — the all-night food street: crayfish, hotpot, grilled fish
timeline.tag: swap→Qianmen/Dashilan if you cannot face another metro ride

days.label: Down the imperial axis

walking_km.how: square→Meridian Gate→Divine Might Gate→Jingshan 3.9 ×1.3 + wandering inside the palace 2.0 + Shichahai and Yandai Xiejie 0.5

days.ribbon: 鲜鱼口 →walk 16′→ 天安门广场 →walk 12′→ 午门 →walk the axis→ 神武门 →walk 10′→ 景山万春亭 →taxi 20′→ 银锭桥 →walk→ 鼓楼
days.rain_alt: the palace's three great halls are all outdoor courtyards. Wet day: stay inside the Treasure Gallery and the Clock Gallery (both inside the palace, small extra fee), then Beihai Park's Round City, then the National Museum of China.
days.late_cut: the palace's last entry is the hard wall — everything after Jingshan is cuttable. Cut Shichahai first, then Jingshan.

timeline.what: Walk 鲜鱼口 → 天安门广场 Tiananmen Square · 1.1 km · 16 min · security check at the square's south entrance
Tiananmen Square 天安门广场 — the square, Tiananmen Gate, the Monument to the People's Heroes, the Great Hall of the People from outside
timeline.note: Passport-controlled entry with airport-grade screening. Allow 20 min for the queue. If the reservation failed, walk around the east side to the palace's ticket gate instead.

timeline.what: Walk 天安门广场 → 午门 Meridian Gate · 0.6 km · 12 min
The Forbidden City 故宫 — in at the Meridian Gate, then the outer court: the Gate of Supreme Harmony and the three great halls straight down the axis
timeline.note: 8:30-16:30 from 1 Nov, last ticket 15:30, last entry 15:40. Closed Mondays — which is why this sits on a Tuesday. Entry ONLY at the Meridian Gate, exit only at the north; you cannot double back. Passport checked at the gate against the booking.

timeline.what: Walk the imperial axis 午门 → 神武门 · 1.3 km inside the walls · no doubling back, the gates are one-way
The inner court and the eastern palaces — the Palace of Heavenly Purity, the Treasure Gallery and the Nine-Dragon Screen, out through the Gate of Divine Might
timeline.price: ¥10 Treasure Gallery (on top of the ¥40 entry)
timeline.note: Same anchor as the block above, split by the axis walk. Last ticket 15:30, last entry 15:40; the palace clears at 16:30.

timeline.what: Walk 神武门 → 景山万春亭 Jingshan (south gate + the climb) · 0.6 km · 10 min
Lunch — the small restaurants on Jingshan Qianjie and Wusi Dajie · jianbing, noodles, a courtyard cafe
Jingshan Park 景山公园 — climb the coal hill to the Wanchun Pavilion for the only free view down the whole golden-roofed axis you just walked
timeline.note: 06:30-20:00 (1 Nov-31 Mar), last entry 19:30. The climb is 10 minutes of steps. Best light is late afternoon, looking south.

timeline.what: Taxi/metro 景山万春亭 → 银锭桥 Silver Ingot Bridge · 1.2 km · ~20 min
Shichahai / Houhai 后海 — the lake ring, the Silver Ingot Bridge, then Yandai Xiejie 烟袋斜街 into the Drum Tower hutongs at sunset (16:58)
timeline.note: Rickshaw touts on the bridge quote per person and change the price mid-ride — walk.

timeline.what: Walk 银锭桥 → 烟袋斜街 → 鼓楼 Drum Tower · 0.4 km
Last dinner — the hutong restaurants around the Drum Tower / Nanluoguxiang's side lanes (avoid the main drag)

days.label: Homeward
days.ribbon: 鲜鱼口 →Airport Express / car 75′→ PEK T3 →Korean Air→ Seoul ICN →→ JFK (same calendar day)
days.late_cut: if the departure is after 15:00, the Temple of Heaven park (06:30 open, ¥15) or Beihai Park fits before you leave — both are 20 min from Qianmen and neither needs a booking.

timeline.what: Leave the hotel. The formula, not a guessed clock time: departure minus 3 h international check-in minus 75 min door-to-terminal.
Metro Line 2 鲜鱼口 → 东直门, Airport Express → 首都机场 T3 · ~65 min · ¥30. With bags a car is ¥130-170 and 60-80 min — but the airport road jams hard 06:00-09:00 and 16:00-19:00.

brief.visa: US passport → a Chinese tourist visa (L) is REQUIRED for this trip. The 240-hour visa-free transit that US citizens can use needs an onward ticket to a THIRD country (A → China → B); JFK → China → JFK is A → China → A and does not qualify. Since 2024-01-01, L-visa applications filed in the US no longer require a round-trip ticket, hotel booking, itinerary or invitation letter; most US applicants receive a 10-year multiple-entry visa. Apply via the COVA online form, then submit the passport in person at the Chinese Visa Application Service Center. Fee reduced through 2026-12-31 (⚠️ exact amount unverified — read it at the link on the checklist); express service +$25. Passport: 6+ months validity, 2 blank pages. Start 8 weeks out. Source: Embassy of the PRC in the USA, us.china-embassy.gov.cn, checked 2026-08-15.
brief.holidays: date.nager.at/PublicHolidays/2026/CN returns six national holidays for 2026 (1 Jan · 17 Feb Spring Festival · 1 May · 19 Jun Dragon Boat · 25 Sep Mid-Autumn · 1 Oct National Day). NONE falls in 11-18 November — the window is deliberately clean. What the feed cannot see and this plan handles instead: the SEASONAL SWITCH on 15/16 November. Mutianyu, the Terracotta Army and the Shaanxi History Museum all change to shorter winter hours mid-trip, and the plan's times are written per-day against the correct side of that boundary.
brief.weather: Same dates last year (Open-Meteo archive, 2025-11-11→18): Beijing 4–17 °C by day, −2 to +4 °C at night, zero precipitation all week; Xi'an 6–18 °C by day, −2 to +7 °C at night, 2 mm on the 16th–17th. Expect a cold snap around the 16th–17th (Beijing dropped to 3.7 °C max last year on that date). Daylight is short: Beijing sunrise ≈06:55, sunset ≈16:52. Dress in layers with a windproof shell — the Great Wall ridge and the Xi'an wall are both fully exposed. Beijing air quality can spike in November heating season; pack an N95 if you are sensitive.
brief.money: Effectively cashless. Alipay and WeChat Pay both accept a foreign Visa/Mastercard directly, no Chinese bank account; verified foreign users can transact up to $5,000 per payment as of early 2026. Alipay is the easier of the two to set up from abroad. Set BOTH up before you fly — verification wants SMS. Foreign cards work at big hotels and almost nowhere else; ATMs at Bank of China and ICBC take foreign cards. Carry ¥500-1,000 cash as the fallback that never fails.
brief.connectivity: ⚠️ The single biggest practical trap on this trip, and the one thing the map links in this plan depend on: Google Maps, Google Search, Gmail, WhatsApp, Instagram and X are all blocked inside mainland China. EVERY hop link in this plan is a Google Maps URL and will fail on a Chinese local SIM. Two fixes, in order: (1) buy a ROAMING travel eSIM (Airalo/Holafly/Saily class) which routes through an offshore gateway and leaves Google working — ≈$15-25 for 8 days, this is the recommendation; (2) install a paid VPN BEFORE departure (their websites are blocked from inside). Third, unconditional safety net: the trip KML that ships with this plan (china.kml) opens offline in Maps.me / Organic Maps / Gaia, and Amap 高德 or Baidu Maps are the apps that actually work locally — both have partial English. Do not plan to download anything after you land.
brief.safety: Beijing and Xi'an are both very safe for a solo traveller at night by any international standard; violent crime against tourists is rare and both cities' central districts are lit and busy until late. The real risks are commercial: the 'tea house' and 'art student' scams around Tiananmen and Wangfujing (a stranger practising English invites you for tea, then the bill is ¥2,000), unlicensed taxis at PEK and Xi'an North (use DiDi or the official rank — never accept a ride from someone approaching you inside the terminal), and fake 游5 buses to the Terracotta Army. Every night in this plan ends within a 15-minute walk or one metro ride of the hotel, and no leg requires a dark walk through an unlit area. Emergency: 110 police, 120 ambulance, 119 fire.
brief.insurance: Travel medical insurance with evacuation cover, bought with the flight. Chinese public hospitals bill foreigners up front, in cash or by card, before treatment; international clinics (United Family, SOS) are excellent and expensive.
